title: Punitive damages and independent torts
summary: The assigned materials distinguish compensatory contract relief from punishment and from separately actionable tort conduct.
notes: White rejects punishment for the malicious contract breach presented. The accompanying notes discuss exceptional tort settings and evolving decisions, including insurance and alleged bad-faith denials of contractual obligations. Those historical examples should not be compressed into either “punitive damages always follow bad faith” or a statement that no conduct connected to a contract could ever support punitive relief.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 30–34. Open assigned page 30.
